claims.statement: Data/Item/ItemDrop.txt is a real file present in Blood Moon's actual server distribution.
claims.sourceLocation: Deploy/Predeploy-Snapshots/20260730-season6-scope-cleanup/.../Data/Item/ItemDrop.txt (confirmed byte-identical to live production 2026-08-17 and to a 2026-08-16/17 14-day-apart comparison, per docs/snapshot-differences.md and docs/configuration-history.md)
claims.notes: sha256 5e29e7cd66e42949613bb51baace0a9c9974decba0c408f1887d5c93a4ccabb2 (local copy read this session)

claims.statement: Blood Moon's real ItemDrop.txt header row has 4 separate DropRate columns named DropRate_AL0, DropRate_AL1, DropRate_AL2, DropRate_AL3 (one per account/VIP tier), not a single DropRate column.
claims.notes: Directly read this session, ground truth, not inferred.

claims.statement: All 92 data lines in Blood Moon's real ItemDrop.txt are commented out (prefixed //), and every DropRate_AL0..AL3 value shown is 0 -- the per-item VIP drop-rate table is entirely inert/unused on Blood Moon.
claims.notes: Matches the prior session's independent finding in docs/drop-system-analysis.md ("100% desativada") -- now directly re-confirmed by reading the raw file this session rather than trusting the paraphrase alone.

claims.statement: The ProjectGamers/eMuGS vendor engine added 4 VIP-tier DropRate columns to ItemDrop.txt (replacing a single DropRate column) in an update the vendor labeled 7.0.
claims.notes: VERIFIED this session: Blood Moon's real file header exactly matches this claim's described post-update structure (see CLAIM-002). This is the ITEMDROP_CLAIM = CONFIRMED result from Phase 2 Part K.

claims.statement: The vendor's own ItemDrop.htm tutorial document (as normalized in docs/vendor-tutorials-knowledge-extraction.md) lists ItemDrop.txt's fields as a single 'DropRate' column, not 4 VIP-tier columns.
claims.providerVersion: pre-7.0 (inferred from column mismatch, see CONFLICT-001)
claims.confidence: CONFIRMED_VENDOR_DOC (as a claim about the tutorial's content) / the claim itself is now known stale relative to the real file
claims.notes: See CONFLICT-001 in knowledge-conflicts.json. This is a genuine version-difference finding, not an error in either document -- the tutorial HTML simply predates the 7.0 column change that the real file already reflects.

claims.statement: Custom Bot Store is a static NPC that sells a fixed list of items for zen and/or Cash, configured via Data/Custom/ text files.
claims.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-26: real file downloaded and read. Bot index 0 ('Luffen', '.::CASH STORE::.') is ACTIVE (not commented), placed at map 0 (Lorencia), coords 141/134 -- this is a genuinely LIVE, deployed feature on Blood Moon, not just a template. Also refines CLAIM-007's slot mapping: real header confirms slot 2 = Helm (the video was unclear on this slot).

claims.statement: Custom Bot Store's shop display grid has a physical size limit that can silently truncate configured items larger than 1x1 (e.g. a wing), even when the configured item-slot list is not full.

verificationTargets.path: a configured Blood Moon CustomBotStore instance, if one exists

claims.notes: Demonstrated live in the video (3 configured wings rendered as only 2).

claims.statement: Custom Bot Trader exchanges one player item for a fixed, pre-configured reward item, gated by a configurable success-rate percentage; on failure the input item is lost with no refund.
claims.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-26: real file downloaded and read. Both configured bots (BotTrade1, BotTrade2) have Enabled=0 -- structurally present but currently DISABLED on Blood Moon. Real mix data ('WingBK' 50% success, 'WingBK2' 100% success) is essentially the vendor's own demo/template data, matching the video's live example almost exactly -- suggests this was deployed but never customized or turned on. File LastWriteTimeUtc = 2023-08-08T05:14:32Z, one day after the tutorial video's 2023-08-07 publish date.

claims.statement: Custom Bot Trader supports a maximum of 30 bot instances of that type per server.
claims.confidence: CONFIRMED_RUNTIME (comment present) / CONFIRMED_VENDOR_VIDEO (30 is the actual enforced max, not just documented)
claims.notes: Vendor states the same 30-instance cap applies to CustomBotTrader, CustomBotBuffer, and CustomBotFusion. The real CustomBotTrader.txt's own header comment confirms 'BotIndex = Index do bot, Max: 30 bots', matching the video -- though only 2 of the 30 possible slots are actually configured on Blood Moon.

claims.statement: Custom Bot Fusion transfers Luck/Skill/Excellent-option rolls from a source item to a target item, at a configurable success rate; on success the source item loses its transferred options.
claims.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-26: real file downloaded and read. Both configured bots (BotFusion1 at Lost Tower, BotFusion2 at Lorencia) have Enabled=0 -- structurally present but currently DISABLED on Blood Moon, same pattern as CustomBotTrader. File also preserves a raw text-encoding artifact worth keeping as-is: the Portuguese balloon text 'Fusão de Items Losttower' has a corrupted accent byte on disk ('Fus?o'), genuinely present in the file, not a transcription error on this sweep's part.

claims.statement: Custom Bot Fusion's real config field is named OnlySameType (not 'BotIndexOnly' as this sweep's initial transcript-based normalization guessed) -- when 1, restricts fusion to items of the same equipment category (e.g. sword-with-sword only); when 0, any category may be mixed. A separate DestinyLower flag additionally restricts fusion to cases where the destination item's level is within +/-10 of the source item's level.
claims.sourceLocation: Data/Custom/CustomBotFusion.txt, section 5 header comment: 'AcceptOnlySameType = Only Accept for example Swords with Swords, and not Swords with Axes' / 'OnlyIfDestinyLower = Only Accept if destiny item level is lower or equals than source item level +10 and -10'
claims.notes: CORRECTION, not a source conflict: the original claim's field name came from an imperfect YouTube auto-transcript ('Bolt index... only semi') that this sweep interpreted as 'BotIndexOnly'. The real file confirms the actual field is 'OnlySameType', and reveals a second related field (DestinyLower) the video's audio didn't clearly convey. This is a good example of why real-config verification matters even for claims that already sounded plausible.

claims.statement: The vendor's GameMaster.txt file has a Section 1 (in addition to the existing GM-commands Section 0) that whitelists specific account logins, by account level, for access to a specific Game Server instance.

The vendor explicitly warns against copying the Data/Command and Data/Event folders when replicating configuration from a secondary/test Game Server to the main Game Server, because these folders are legitimately different per server instance.
claims.notes: This is an operator-safety claim about vendor engine behavior in general, not a Blood-Moon-specific fact -- not something to 'verify against config', but worth preserving as an operational constraint for any future Blood Moon config-deployment tooling.

claims.statement: The EuSanTiago channel's featured upgrade system (Legendary Craft, Elite tier, Shiny Imperial stones, Tol booster, Blaz currency) describes RealMU, a different MU Online private server, not Blood Moon.
claims.notes: MUST NOT be promoted to BLOODMOON_LIKELY or higher under any circumstance -- recorded specifically to prevent future contamination, per docs/knowledge/source-authority.md.

claims.statement: Blood Moon's real Data/Custom/CustomBotBuffer.txt has its entire bot-placement table (section 1) commented out -- zero active buffer-bot entries, even though the cost/item-requirement/skill sections (2-4) below it are fully configured with 6 class-specific buffer templates (SM/BK/ELF/DL/SUM/RF).
claims.notes: Discovered opportunistically this session while verifying the sibling Store/Trader/Fusion configs -- no video transcript exists yet for CustomBotBuffer beyond the 3 pre-existing project-gamers-oficial transcripts from an earlier session (sK5QGl2ykQc, per transcripts-status.tsv), so this claim has no KI-* video source, only the real config.

claims.statement: Of the 4 vendor static-NPC bot systems present on Blood Moon (Store, Trader, Fusion, Buffer), only CustomBotStore is currently deployed active (1 live NPC, 'Luffen', a cash shop in Lorencia). Trader, Fusion, and Buffer all exist as configured files but have zero active/enabled entries.
claims.sourceLocation: Data/Custom/CustomBotStore.txt, CustomBotTrader.txt, CustomBotFusion.txt, CustomBotBuffer.txt (all read this session)
claims.notes: This is a synthesis claim across CLAIM-006/008/010/016 -- recorded separately because the PATTERN (most vendor bot features get deployed-but-disabled) is itself a notable, general finding about how Blood Moon adopts vendor updates, echoing the same 'present but inert' pattern already independently found for ItemDrop.txt (CLAIM-003). Worth re-checking if this generalizes further as more Data/Custom files get read.

claims.statement: The Custom Drop Reward system grants a chance-based currency reward (Ruud and/or WCoin/PCPoint) when a player drops a specifically-configured 'Box' item on the ground, with per-item success percentage and a min/max or fixed reward amount.

Update 6.8 extends the EventItemBag end-of-event drop mechanism (already used by Blood Castle and Illusion Temple) to Devil Square, adding 7 configurable sub-indices (one per Devil Square level/stage).
claims.notes: Data/EventItemBagManager.txt itself is already a known, real Blood Moon file (referenced in drop-rate-system.json's relations.related_configs as 'parallel system, not the normal drop path') -- this claim adds behavioral detail (which events use it, and how) not yet cross-checked against its actual content.

claims.statement: Update 6.9 adds 'Reward Level' and 'Reward Points' columns to CustomMonster.txt, letting a specific monster grant direct character levels or a custom points currency on kill, in addition to the pre-existing Quest/GoblinPoint/Reset/MasterReset reward columns.
claims.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-26 (Phase 2 continuation): real file downloaded (modified 2026-08-15, 11 days before this sweep) and read. Header confirms RewardLevel and RewardPoints columns exactly as described, plus reveals a much richer column set the video didn't demo: MapNumber, MaxLife, DamageMin/Max, Defense, AttackRate, DefenseRate, ExperienceRate, KillMessage, InfoMessage, SummonMonster, SummonMonsterCount, RewardValue1-3, RewardReset, RewardMasterReser (sic, real typo in the file), AlertMessageAttackSwitch/Time. All 7 configured monster entries (custom indices 275/361/459/561/295/801/802) are commented out -- 100% inert, matching the SAME 'present but disabled' pattern independently found in ItemDrop.txt, CustomBotTrader, CustomBotFusion, and CustomBotBuffer (5th confirmed instance of this pattern -- see CLAIM-017's note, worth treating as an established Blood Moon operational characteristic now, not a coincidence).

claims.statement: The vendor recommends CustomMonster.txt's Reward Points column for building dedicated 'build point' farming maps aimed at level-400+ characters, typically combined with open PvP on the same map.
claims.notes: Vendor recommendation/use-case, not a verifiable config fact -- recorded as a FACT (this is what the vendor recommends) not a Blood-Moon-specific RECOMMENDATION (whether Blood Moon actually does this is unknown, no evidence either way).

claims.statement: Pressing H shows a panel of currently-active event schedules, gated by a CustomEventTimer=1 flag in Data/Custom -- only enabled events appear in the list.
Custom Event PvP All is a GM-opened, player-joined kill-all PvP event where participants cannot attack each other until the GM closes/starts the event.
claims.notes: Demonstrated live: 2 characters could not damage each other after joining but before the GM started the event.

claims.statement: Custom Event PvP All scores kills at +2 points and deaths at -1 point by default, both independently configurable (death penalty can be set to 0).
claims.notes: Demonstrated live and matched exactly: 4 kills + 1 death = 7 points (8-1); 1 kill + 4 deaths = 0 or negative, displayed as no ranking.

claims.statement: Custom Event PvP All grants independently configurable currency rewards for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place finishers, drawn from multiple possible currencies (a ranking/honor-specific currency, WCoin, Gold, GoblinPoint).
claims.notes: Exact currency names uncertain due to ASR transcription quality on this segment ('Arranquei honra' likely a mistranscription of a ranking/honor currency name) -- flagged as lower-confidence on the specific currency names, though the mechanism itself (multi-currency, per-rank reward) is clear.

claims.statement: Across every vendor-provided Data/Custom system independently verified against Blood Moon's real config so far (ItemDrop.txt, CustomBotTrader.txt, CustomBotFusion.txt, CustomBotBuffer.txt, CustomMonster.txt), the file is present with the correct/current column structure but every configured data row is commented out or Enabled=0 -- only CustomBotStore.txt (CLAIM-006/017) is an exception, with 1 genuinely active entry.
claims.sourceLocation: Data/Item/ItemDrop.txt, Data/Custom/CustomBotTrader.txt, CustomBotFusion.txt, CustomBotBuffer.txt, CustomMonster.txt -- all read directly this session
claims.notes: 5 independent files now show the same pattern (1 exception: CustomBotStore is live). At this sample size it looks like a genuine operational characteristic of how Blood Moon's administrator(s) adopt vendor updates -- files get copied in during an update but are rarely individually enabled/customized/activated unless there's a specific reason (as with the Store). Sample is still small (5 of 90 files in Data/Custom) and drawn non-randomly (files this sweep happened to have video sources for) -- NOT yet strong enough to claim this holds for all 90 files, but strong enough to flag as a real pattern worth testing further.
